steps.headline: This is what done means for Assistant settings.

rows.statement: One Assistant settings row in the Settings drawer replaces Model Providers, Defaults, Permissions and Specialists.
The Assistant settings row shows the current default, plus a red dot when a provider is broken.
The row opens one wide window: a list of pages on the left, the chosen page on the right.
The list is five flat pages: General, Cloud providers, Local models, Permissions, Specialists.
rows.note: i think defaul model and default project folder should both have correctly styled dropdowns. the title of project folder should be "Show Project Folder". websearch should not be a bare header, but a card that contains the tavily/exa cards. tight spacing on it.

rows.statement: Any connected model, Claude, ChatGPT, OpenRouter or a downloaded local one, can be set as the default.
rows.note: just call this Default Model. line below should say "This model will be pre-filled in the model picker, but you may still switch models at any time

rows.statement: General's first row is Default model, saying the pick is pre-filled but switchable; web search keys sit at the bottom.
rows.note: add mirror line in project folder when we add dropdown.

rows.statement: The folder row is called Default project folder.
The default folder control is the same folder picker the new conversation form uses, folder icon and all.
Open, it lists your saved folders with a tick on the one in use, and Browse for folder at the bottom.
rows.note: i think on this surface (not in new session menu or elsewhere) the width of the selection menu should match the dropdown card, and the project name/filepath/etc should be in-line together.

rows.statement: In this panel the open folder list is as wide as the control, one line per folder.
Cloud providers stacks the Claude Code, ChatGPT and OpenRouter cards on one page, with your own API keys below.
rows.note: we should also have a white "My Account" page button that outlinks to the relevant provider's webpage. should be at the top right when signed in. also i thought we were supposed to make the claude code card mirror the gpt card with usage limits and such and a sign out button.

rows.statement: Claude Code's card matches ChatGPT's with limit bars and Sign out, and every signed-in card has My Account.
Sign out on the Claude Code card explains where to sign out, and signs nothing out.
rows.note: skip the first section of text "youcoded cannot clear it for you"

rows.statement: That sign-out popup is one sentence saying where to go and what to type.
Permissions holds Claude Code's Skip Permissions switch first, then the three modes and Always-allowed list for other providers.
rows.note: change copy. that should be "Enable Skip Permissions Mode?" with copy that says" Allows you to toggle claude code's --dangerously-skip-permissions flag when creating a session. Claude won't ask before taking action

rows.statement: The Advanced list of protection overrides is gone from the app.
rows.note: see previous slide. i think we should drop this altogether

rows.statement: Any protection override someone had switched on is turned off when this ships.
The switch is titled Enable Skip Permissions Mode? with a hint about Claude Code's skip-permissions flag when starting a session.
rows.note: remove the current red banner. replace it with a blocking popup that requires to acknowledge whatever working claude code itself uses for the skip permissions confirmation screen. tick a box saying they ackowleding they use it at their own risk.

rows.statement: Turning Skip Permissions on stops you with a popup you must tick to confirm; turning it off is instant.
rows.note: this copy is weird. way too much gray text. cahng to something like "When you begin a session in skip permissions mode,Claude Code will not ask before taking actions or running commands. You should be cautious when attempting to use this mode with Haiku- or Sonnnet- class models.

rows.statement: That popup is one short paragraph in ordinary text, cautioning about Haiku- and Sonnet-class models.
Local models has a whole page: the engine card, the model browser and other local apps.
Specialists is one page: the tier pickers above, the roster below, unchanged.
On a phone the five pages are the first screen, and a page opens with a back arrow.
Android gets the same Assistant settings row and panel now, showing only the pages it can serve.
